newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fazio says flexible labour creates jobs.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fazio says flexible labour creates jobs.

text.p: Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio on Saturday called for a more flexible labour market in Italy and Europe to help create jobs and combat cyclical unemployment.

"In Italy and the other industrial economies, cyclical unemployment is due to the rigidity of companies' overall salary burden, which does not change even when global demand is in a downturn," Fazio said in a speech.
He told a conference in this northeastern town that wages should be more strongly linked to productivity and revenue, saying that "would bring about a better allocation of factors (of production)".
"Wage flexibility...leads to a sort of division of profits and indirectly to the company's goals...it can raise the level of employment," he said.
Fazio said the success of small Italian companies was largely due to a flexible workforce who willingly worked to meet the company's financial goals.

But he said that while recent wage accords have helped to stabilise prices and made Italian industry competitive, they have not reduced unemployment precisely because of the rigidity of the labour market.
